dedupe_keys.name: urban floods case study of chennai nidm disaster and development 2009

description: This case study, contributed by the Chennai city team under an NIDM national coordinated project and published in the journal Disaster and Development in 2009, profiles the causes of urban flooding in Chennai, a very flat coastal city about 6.7 metres above sea level. It tabulates the heaviest one-day rainfalls on record, from 520 millimetres in 1846 to 400 and 320 millimetres in October and December 2005, and describes population growth, densities up to 368 persons per hectare, the five sewerage drainage zones and river and canal encroachment, noting 5,288 families living on the margins of feeder channels. Coverage: one city, historic rainfall to 2005, in narrative and tables. Access: a free PDF; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: only the first part of the article was read, the flood impact and recommendation sections were not inspected, and the figures predate the 2015 floods. It supports drainage network capacity and flood exposure analysis, and relates to the Zhengzhou pluvial flood emergency capacity case study in the catalogue.
